audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Akshan levels 1-4 outright (phases[0..3].side = Akshan) and called the rest Skill, while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Neeko. Every ratings row was set to 7/10 underneath a side that said the enemy was winning.
audit.why: Neeko is at 59.01% over 161 games here, the highest number on this slice. Heroic Swing needs terrain to hook and is 18s at rank 1, so in an open mid lane Akshan's escape simply is not available; Neeko's E at 1000 range outranges his 800 grapple. The lane only levels out when his first item arrives.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side = Neeko, phases[5].side = Skill, phases[6].side = Neeko, with the whys rewritten to match and ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes ended 'Luden's makes the package lethal' on a stage the chart calls Skill — the first-item window is the one stage in this lane that is genuinely even, not a Neeko spike.
audit.why: Akshan's first item brings crit poke online while Neeko's brings burst; content spikes[2] already calls it a coinflip decided by whether E catches the grapple. Naming Neeko's item as the lethal one contradicts the row directly above it.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is the kill pattern; level 6 answers his swing; first items turn it into a coinflip.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (defect 3) and described Heroic Swing only as 'his swing engage/escape'. Nowhere did the page state the ability's terrain requirement, its 18s rank-1 cooldown, Avengerang's return damage, or Comeuppance's 2500 range.
audit.why: The terrain requirement is the whole matchup: Riot's text says he fires the hook into terrain and swings around it. In open lane he has no engage and no exit, which is why fighting position matters more here than cooldown counting — and neither fact was on the page.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Heroic Swing 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 plus the terrain requirement, Avengerang 9s down to 5s with damage on the return, and Comeuppance 100/85/70 at 2500 range.
sources: enemyKit Q cd 9/8/7/6/5 and 'damage going out and coming back'

audit.whatIsWrong: Going Rogue's camouflage is never mentioned, and Neeko has no reveal anywhere in her kit.
audit.why: The feed flags stealth-needs-vision. W drops to 2s at rank 5 with no mana cost, so once he maxes it the disappearing is close to permanent — Control Wards and a sweeper are load-bearing, not optional.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now states the camouflage decides where he appears and names the Control Ward and sweeper as the fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dirty Fighting's shield is absent from the page, and report[8].t instead told the reader to buy anti-heal 'into his sustain' — Akshan has no heal in his kit at all.
audit.why: Every third hit from his attacks and abilities shields him when the target is a champion. That shield lands inside exactly the window Neeko's root-bloom is trying to burst through, so it changes the all-in maths; Grievous Wounds does nothing to it.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now reads 'Break the Dirty Fighting shield before you commit.'
sources: enemyKit P text and shield flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ability name in the content layer: spikes[0].text says 'Avengerous Q'. The ability is Avengerang.
audit.why: The kit file is authority on names. 'Avengerous' does not exist.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed on four bullets: dosFull[1].d (title 'Disguise in the wave when he hits 6') carried tradeGood; dontsFull[1].d (title 'Shove past river without the root banked') carried the clone paragraph; dontsFull[2].d (title 'Greed blooms at half HP') carried tradeBad verbatim; dontsFull[0].d was a name-swap template that explained nothing about the title.
audit.why: Defect 2 — the title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten to answer their own titles from Akshan's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood claimed 'the full package is half a bar at level 3' — magnitude with no source (defect 6) — and never mentioned that Avengerang hits twice.
audit.why: Riot's text: the boomerang deals damage going out and coming back. Standing still after your own trade to watch the bloom is what collects the return hit.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the sequence plus the exit cue: step out of the boomerang's return.

audit.why: The content layer claims 'E-root him mid-grapple to cancel his Swing'. Riot's text says only that he can jump off early or is knocked off by colliding with champions or terrain — it does not say a root cancels the swing. The claim is inherited and unverifiable from the kits.
audit.corrected: Left untouched in the content layer, and not repeated in any new text I wrote. Recorded in unverified.

Level chart: the full layer handed Akshan levels 1-4 outright in a matchup Neeko wins 59.01% of, while the content layer said Neeko — proposed as one atomic group. report[8].t prescribed anti-heal against a champion with no heal in his kit; replaced with the Dirty Fighting shield, which is the real burst-window problem.
